messages:
Ruth (Finance): Heads up  today's provider invoice has a new SKU line called 'ML Model Runtime Surcharge' tied to GPU instances. Delta ~$13,200 and it's not in our price table. Anyone introduced a third-party runtime? :thinking_face:
Ibrahim (Product): We did a pilot with vendor 'VertexModels' for their optimized runtime in a few workloads last month. Did we get a marketplace license line?
Carmen (VendorRelations): Checking vendor contract now. We have a trial addendum but no published marketplace surcharge in the contract. Can you paste the invoice rows?
Ruth (Finance): Excerpt from provider bill export:
```
project_id | sku_description                 | usage_start           | cost
search-prod | GPU hours                      | 2026-12-06T01:00:00Z | 4200.00
search-prod | ML Model Runtime Surcharge     | 2026-12-06T01:00:00Z | 4300.00
analytics   | GPU hours                      | 2026-12-06T02:30:00Z | 3800.00
analytics   | ML Model Runtime Surcharge     | 2026-12-06T02:30:00Z | 4100.00
```
Lines show the surcharge paired with GPU usage. No internal cost_center for the surcharge; provider billed it as separate SKU.
Luca (Eng-ML): That matches the days we ran the VertexModels optimized worker on search-prod and analytics. We installed their runtime via the marketplace image last month for the pilot. I didn't realize it would bill as an extra SKU.
Priya (Legal): Did we consent to marketplace billing on install? Often marketplace images include a separate charge. Contract addendum should show if it's billable or covered in trial.
Carmen (VendorRelations): I have the trial addendum — it states "no runtime surcharge during 30-day trial". The pilot started Nov 20 and ended Dec 4, so the invoice period Dec 6 shouldn't have trial protections. But the provider SKU name suggests marketplace metering. Need to confirm activation date in vendor portal.
CostBot: Note: provider SKU-level surcharges may be billed directly on cloud invoice; retro tags won't remove provider charges.
Ruth (Finance): Financial options: A) Backcharge to the teams that ran the marketplace image (search & analytics) B) Absorb in a central "vendor-experiment" budget for the pilot period C) Open vendor/provider dispute and request credit if this was unexpected per trial/RSAs.
Ibrahim (Product): Product prefers option C first. If vendor confirms surcharge post-trial, we can consider B while dispute is open, then reconcile. We ran this as product-led experiment.
Priya (Legal): I'll escalate contract review. If the marketplace billing was enabled by the marketplace image activation date being set to Nov 25, and trial expired Dec 4, legal can argue the vendor should have notified us of impending transition. I'll need vendor billing logs and marketplace activation timestamps.
Carmen (VendorRelations): I'll pull vendor portal logs and marketplace activation events. Also opening a vendor support ticket asking for retroactive credit if the surcharge was enabled without notice. Ticket: VM-2026-331 (I'll paste link).
Luca (Eng-ML): For remediation, I can roll back the image on analytics/search-prod to the vendor-free base image to stop further surcharges. Stopping rollouts now.
Ruth (Finance): Please snapshot provider invoice and raw export to gs://finance/snapshots/1935004321-vertex-surcharge.csv before any further changes. I'll draft an internal memo and provisional chargeback plan.
Ibrahim (Product): Owners: Ruth -> snapshot + provisional invoice + decide interim funding; Carmen -> vendor logs + support ticket; Priya -> contract review & escalation; Luca -> rollback images + list of affected deployments. Target: initial update by EOD 2026-12-06.
Carmen (VendorRelations): Vendor ticket opened and assigned. Logged evidence: invoice excerpt + portal activation timestamps (pending). Requesting expedited review.
Priya (Legal): If vendor refuses credit, we'll review SLA and communication obligations. If vendor metered via marketplace product terms, we may still have grounds if activation notification was missing.
Ruth (Finance): Interim finance stance: put the surcharge on a suspense internal account and don't pass to customers. If vendor credits us, we'll reverse. If not, decide between backcharge to product teams or absorb under "vendor-experiments". We'll need final decision before month close.
Luca (Eng-ML): Rollbacks started. I'll post the list of effected pod-revisions and namespaces in a follow-up message.
Ibrahim (Product): Also log this for the product experimentation playbook: marketplace images should have an explicit billing-awareness checklist before rollout.
CostBot: Reminder: retro tags update internal attribution only; provider invoice disputes must go through vendor support.
Ruth (Finance): Snapshot saved: gs://finance/snapshots/1935004321-vertex-surcharge.csv. I'll post the provisional internal memo here when ready. Thanks team.
